sourceClassBindingRule.statement: Section I sourceClass is MECHANICALLY BOUND by PI-7 from the final Git-bound sourceClass closure. For every section I edge consuming a selected-fact sourceRef, the coder copies the binding record's sectionIFill exactly: sourceClass where the state is ASSIGNED, otherwise the fail-closed state verbatim. Reclassification, inference from documentaryIdentity (R-FORM), conversion of a fail-closed state into ASSIGNED, and invention of a fact-level sourceClass where several supplying records differ are all FORBIDDEN.
sourceClassBindingRule.multiSourceRefRule: R-EDGE: one section I edge per class-bearing support record. Where a fact's supplying sourceRefs are lawfully separable class-bearing records carrying different classes, the coder emits separate section I edges, one per support record, each carrying its own singular sourceClass, sharing the same M binding and relationInstanceId. A non-ASSIGNED binding never counts toward srcDiv (R-COUNT PRE-5) and is never converted to ASSIGNED.
sourceClassBindingRule.precedenceOverSidecarNote: PI-3's sourceClassResolution block (NOT_MECHANICALLY_BOUND_BY_STAGE_1 / CODER_JUDGMENT_REQUIRED_UNCHANGED) remains a true statement about Stage-1: Stage-1 does not bind a section I sourceClass value. From this correction onward the sourceClass VALUE is bound mechanically by PI-7; where the two surfaces appear to conflict, PI-7 controls the value and PI-3 controls documentary identity and provenance.
sourceClassBindingRule.pilotObservation: In the frozen pilot surface no multi-sourceRef fact has an ASSIGNED supplying record (both multi-sourceRef facts are all-OUTSIDE_FROZEN_VOCABULARY on every segment), so no edge-spanning separation case arises in this pilot; the rule is stated for mechanical completeness and creates no new semantics.
